source: Marina CG tour Part 1 (1080p copy), 305-360 s at 4 fps. Clip A = foyer pan frames 29-62 (sfm-work/rooms/stairs-a, gate 3/3). Clip B = climb frames 116-187 (sfm-work/rooms/stairs, gate 6/6; trimmed before the 'Living Room' title that fades in from ~192). Layout: Marina's main-floor overhead, Part 1 frame 216 (same extraction).
scale: clip A door (closet under the arch), robust slab-interior fit, 0.309-0.315 units over 3 frames: 6.47 m/unit at 80 in. All lengths at 80 in; multiply by 0.975 for 78 in.

methods: image: 13 nosings on the stringer in frame 31 fit a 1-D projective (equal-spacing) model, rms 3.2 px; 14 with one hidden is rejected (rms 13 px, max 30)
3D: clip B tread heights, foyer floor to the top level = 12.95 x rise
risers_floor_to_landing.kind: two methods on the same footage; agree

rise_m.method: clip A riser tops (vertical only), door-scaled

pitch_deg.method: tools/sfm/stair_pitch.py: vanishing points of verticals and the skirting/handrail lines, 3 gated frames (116/118/120); +-10% focal moves it 0.9 deg; self-test reads synthetic 30/35/40 deg within 0.1 and rejects a one-line image

landing_height_m.method: 13 x rise; the landing balustrade base reads 2.32 m above the foyer floor in clip A (3 frames, 1-3 cm spread), which includes its shoe rail

tread_band_width_m.method: clip B carpet-tread extent across 10 steps (wall-to-rail width a little more)
tread_band_width_m.kind: measured (lateral to the camera, not affected by the depth stretch)

layout.flight_1: straight, along the foyer's left (photo) wall, rising from the front of the house toward the rear
layout.landing: full width of the foyer along the rear wall: picture and table ahead of flight 1, big window on its right part; balustrade along its front edge facing down into the foyer (clip B top-down: the rail turns 90 deg at the landing newel and runs ~2.8 m)
layout.in_upstairs_plan: landing at the west (rear) end of main_stair_opening, spanning its 2.83 m width; flight 1 along the south side
layout.flight_2: NOT in Marina's main-floor model and never filmed in Part 1 or Part 2: authored (see docs/STATUS.md)

rejected: rise/going from the 3D point clouds: 0.44-0.52 (24-27 deg). Both clips look along the flight, and VGGT stretches that depth direction by ~1.35 relative to height; tread/riser normals also come out 75-80 deg apart. Use 3D for vertical and lateral sizes only on stairs.

door height from edge pixels (door_scale.py) on this door: 14% short, because the slab is recessed under an arch and the top-edge pixel takes the arch's depth. Re-checked the upstairs doors with the robust method: Kevin +0.8%, parents +0.6% (inside the 78-80 in bracket).
